newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No EU decision on BA/AMR seen before September.
newsitem.headline: No EU decision on BA/AMR seen before September.

text.p: The European Commission is unlikely to rule before September on British Airways' planned cooperation deal with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, a commission official said Wednesday.
Antitrust officials from the EU's 15 countries are due to discuss the planned tie-up at an advisory meeting July 23, the official said, meaning final clearance is likely to slip into September.

"I think there will be quite a bit of negotiation after the advisory committee, which means that it would be sometime in the autumn that this would finally be decided," said the official, who asked not to be identified by name.
The two airlines plan to coordinate all passenger and cargo arrangements between Europe and the United States, with shared benefits and pooled revenue.

The proposed deal, challenged in July 1996 by the commission, would also involve flight code sharing across the companies' global networks and the setup of a fully reciprocal frequent flyer programme.

British Airways Chief Executive Robert Ayling is due in Brussels on Friday to meet with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, his third trip at least to the European Commission in an effort to secure EU clearance.

The pressure is all on British Airways to offer concessions, the official said, particularly after a U.S. General Accounting Office report urging that six U.S. carriers seeking access to London's Heathrow Airport be granted takeoff and landing slots allowing them 23 daily round trips.

The commission is also investigating the competition effects of Lufthansa's alliance with UAL Corp.'s United Airlines, the one between Dutch airline KLM and Northwest Airlines Corp., and one joining Delta Air Lines Inc., Sabena, Swissair and Austrian Airlines.

The official anticipated that the commission might lump together its decision on BA/American along with a proposal to revise EU slot rules, with a decision on the other alliances following shortly after.
